purpose: G0-DB receipt v2 — supersedes g0-db-receipt.json per Astra Review 6 R6-07. The v1 receipt (a) equated an IN-CONTAINER loopback probe with a host-namespace match, (b) recorded the port-bind failure as if it were a universal cause, and (c) left lifecycle authority ambiguous. All three are corrected here. The v1 file is retained unmodified as history; this receipt is the one source-bindings binds.

cluster.ownership: GENUINELY OWNED — created this session; not the shared dev cluster.
cluster.whyNotTheSharedCluster: Same ruling as v1: 127.0.0.1:5433 (swan-dev-pg) holds prior Coach databases (coach_baseline_gen, coach_emptydb_20260916) and is a shared development resource. Not used.
cluster.loopbackContract: Published as 127.0.0.1:55533->5432/tcp. The listener is host-loopback ONLY (no 0.0.0.0 publication), which is the package's loopback-only trust-listener rule (R6-07: 'do not broaden database access merely to make this sandbox work').
cluster.portSelection: 55433 was attempted first and refused by Windows (excluded port range 55406-55505, netsh excludedportrange). 55533 is outside every listed exclusion. The v1 receipt's four failed ports (55440-55443) sat inside or adjacent to the same reservations.

verifiedIdentity.observedVia: node pg Client from the worktree backend directory — the RUNNER'S NAMESPACE (host process), not docker exec. This is the R6-07 correction: a container-loopback probe and a host match are different network namespaces.
verifiedIdentity.probe: SELECT current_database(), current_user, inet_server_addr(), inet_server_port(); SHOW server_encoding; SHOW data_directory;
verifiedIdentity.serverSideAddress: 172.17.0.4:5432 (the server's own view — container-internal; recorded rather than hidden)
verifiedIdentity.serverVersion: PostgreSQL 17.10 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl, compiled by gcc (Alpine 15.2.0) 15.2.0, 64-bit
verifiedIdentity.statement: Identity observed from the same namespace the runner executes in, over the published loopback port. The host->container reachability that BLOCKED v1 no longer blocks.

r607Corrections.namespaceConflation: v1 line 'observedVia: docker exec … (IN-CONTAINER)' called container-loopback a host match. Corrected: the binding observation for C0 admission is the host-namespace probe above.
r607Corrections.universalCause: v1 recorded 'this session's sandbox forbids binding NEW host ports' as the cause. Adjudication per Astra: the UNIVERSAL cause is UNKNOWN; the measured fact is session-specific (this later session bound 55533 successfully). v1's failed endpoints remain recorded history; the classification 'every possible host port is unusable' is withdrawn.
r607Corrections.runnerTeardownOverstatement: run-contract.json#entryPoints.applicationSuite.why overstated teardown. Fact: backend/run-coach-postgres.mjs releases the LEASE; it contains no cluster-stop operation and never claims to stop PostgreSQL. Cluster startup/shutdown belong to the surrounding operator window (below).
r607Corrections.receiptLifecycleOnStop: v1 claimed stopping the container would invalidate its identity receipt. Corrected: a receipt records an observation; the lifecycle below records the subsequent stop. Observations do not expire when the observed process does.

lifecycle.owner: the agent session (vs-claude) within the operator window Sean authorized by directing this workstream to be finished; Astra R6-07 ruling: 'Must the existing container remain running? No. Preserve the observation and record authorized lifecycle shutdown.'

events.action: stopped swan-coach-owned-20260921 (the v1 cluster: correct identity, NO published host port, unreachable from the runner namespace; docker exit 0)
events.authorization: Astra Review 6 R6-07 lifecycle ruling; identity observation preserved in g0-db-receipt.json (retained).

events.action: verified identity of swan-coach-owned-20260921-host from the runner namespace (this receipt's verifiedIdentity)

lifecycle.shutdownPlan: When the guarded run completes (C0 PASS or a bounded-repair STOP), the operator window stops swan-coach-owned-20260921-host with docker stop and records the timestamp here. The runner itself never stops the cluster.

migrations.reason: C2 slice. Nothing here claims it ran. The reachable target removes the v1 blocker; execution order is C0 admission first.

classification.before: v1: PARTIALLY CLOSED — identity observed in-container; execution BLOCKED by session-specific port binding.
classification.after: CLOSED FOR C0 — owned cluster provisioned, loopback-published, identity verified FROM THE RUNNER NAMESPACE, lifecycle owned and recorded. C1 execution may proceed under the runner's own lease/marker guards.
classification.residual: Production installed-history claims (C2 upgrade equivalence) still require a separately authorized sanitized production receipt; nothing here touches production.
